title: Intra-cardiac Side-Firing Light Catheter for Monitoring Cellular Metabolism using Transmural Absorbance Spectroscopy of Perfused Mammalian Hearts
protocol: Make 4 liters of modified Krebs-Henseleit perfusate.
pH the perfusate to 7.4 at 37 °C with NaOH and HCl.
Filter the perfusate through a 1 µm pore membrane.
Rinse all tubes and chambers of the perfused heart system by running purified water through the system.
Transfer the perfusate into the tank.
Oxygenate the perfusate with 100% O2 using a bubbler while maintaining the temperature at 37 °C using a heated circulating water bath.
Add two 12 µm pore membrane filters and prime the system with the perfusate in Langendorff mode.
Adjust the tubing clamp so that the aortic flow drops to about 10 mL/min.
Anesthetize male New Zealand white rabbits via intramuscular injection of ketamine/acepromazine mixture (10:1).
Administer isoflurane via inhalation for complete anesthetic effect.
Confirm proper depth of anesthesia by toe pinching.
Place a line in the marginal ear vein for drug administration.
Inject 1,500 units (or 1.5 mL) of Heparin and let circulate for 3 minutes.
Double check proper depth of anesthesia.
Euthanize with 6 mEq (or 3 mL) of KCl.
Rapidly open the chest.
Locate the heart’s apex and the aorta.
Cut the aorta as far from the heart as possible.
Cut the pulmonary veins as close to the lungs as possible.
Place the heart in a small beaker of perfusate sitting in a bucket of ice for transportation.
Cannulate and tie the aorta securely, avoiding any bubbles in the aortic line.
Initiate flow at 70 mmHg perfusion pressure by removing the tubing clamp on the aortic line.
Maintain perfusion pressure during surgery and vessel cannulation.
Separate the pulmonary artery from the aorta and other vessels.
Ligate the vena cavae and pulmonary veins.
Remove remaining fat and connective tissue.
Cannulate the pulmonary artery to measure coronary sinus flow rate and oxygen tension.
Discard initial flow out of the heart during preparation to eliminate blood and surgical debris.
Recirculate the perfusate after discarding initial flow for about 10 minutes.
Connect a fiber optic catheter to a high-power fiber-coupled LED white light source.
Cut a small appendage of the left atrium.
Insert the catheter into the left ventricle via the mitral valve.
Rotate the catheter to achieve an illuminated left ventricular free wall.
Position the pickup fiber optic directly opposite the region of maximum illumination at about 1 cm from the heart.
Connect the other end of the pickup fiber to a rapid scanning spectrometer.
Turn off the lights in the experimental area to obtain complete darkness.
Start the custom program incorporating spectrometer drivers for data acquisition and real-time analysis.
Navigate through all prompts, selecting options for perfused heart spectroscopy acquisition mode.
Indicate whether auxiliary data collection is occurring on the next page.
Enter acquisition parameters including location of both chromophores reference spectra and data to be saved.
Enter a bandwidth of 490–630 nm.
Enter a sampling rate of 2 Hz.
Collect a dark current spectrum with the light source off to correct for background signal levels.
Select chromophore references desired for fitting routine.
Adjust position of catheter and pickup fiber to maximize transmitted light in software, focusing on 500 nm region.
Ensure transmitted light is not saturating detector at 600 nm.
Turn off all external light sources and confirm no light is detected by the system.
Initiate data collection by clicking Save Spectra button.
Set current spectrum as control for viewing difference absorbance with future spectra.
Stop recirculating fluid from the heart perfusion.
Inject cyanide (2.5 to 75 mM at pH 7) into the perfusate just before the aortic cannula using a syringe pump.
Monitor cardiac function and optical properties during cyanide infusion.
Continue cyanide infusion until steady state effects on coronary flow, heart rate, and optical transmission through the heart wall are observed.
Stop cyanide infusion after reaching steady state conditions.
Switch bubbling gas from 100% oxygen to 100% nitrogen to remove oxygen from the system.
Simulate a total ischemic/hypoxic condition by stopping the flow after approximately 10 minutes.
Run the program in the perfused heart analysis mode.
Select appropriate spectrometer for data analysis.
Enter the data file path and reference spectra file.
Load pre-saved spectrum of the catheter light source.
Select Read Bin Data option.
Set minimum and maximum wavelength range for data analysis as 490–630 nm.
Return to main menu after setting wavelength range.
Read references used in the analysis from the main menu.
Confirm reference spectra for use in analysis.
Return to main menu after confirming reference spectra.
Select T0 time point as control with a range of 100 points.
Set T1 time point as experimental period at a range of 100 points.
Observe the raw difference spectrum in the Averaged Abs. Spectrum tab.
Select Calculate Fit Coefficients and then click on the Fit Coefficients tab to observe the time course of the reference spectra fit.
Return to the Main Menu and select Calculate Difference Abs.
Select T0 and ΔT1 at all positions.
Observe the fitted spectrum in the Difference Spectrum window and fitting elements in the Reference Weight window.
Repeat this procedure to compare other time points in the experiment.
Return to the Main Menu.
Save data and analysis in a spreadsheet report by typing in a desired name and selecting Save Data for further analysis with other programs.
